note: The sources of the place packs. Every accepted source has an open licence that allows redistribution (checked November 2026; check again when a source changes its terms). Three exceptions, by the owner's decisions of 26 November 2026: chain-locators, facts read from big chains' own store locators (licence store-locator-facts); government facts used regardless of a copy's missing licence or a site's own terms (licence government-facts: the Social Security offices' ArcGIS copy, US cities' and counties' open-data layers of public places, Recreation.gov's RIDB export, California's health and human services files); and facts from local directories and lookups (licence directory-facts: tourism boards' Simpleview and Tempest listings, chambers' ChamberMaster directories, Hotfrog's business listings, businesses' own homepages, Yellow Pages lookups of businesses already in the packs; since 27 November 2026 also campus and indoor maps' buildings and accessibility features, map-vendors, hospitals' and clinics' accessibility facts from insurers' public provider directories and hospitals' own pages, health-access, and museums' accessibility facts from their own pages, museum-access); since 27 November 2026 the government facts also include street-access and street-access-navigation (cities' and transportation departments' accessible pedestrian signals and curb ramps, transit agencies' elevator lists, Amtrak's station information). url fields marked verify: true were written from the publisher's documented pattern and must be checked at the first build (a failed download only leaves that layer out and is listed in the build summary). store-locator-facts.name: Facts read from each chain's own public store locator (store positions, addresses, telephone numbers, web pages and opening hours). The chains grant no licence; facts are not protected by copyright in the United States (Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service, 499 U.S. 340, 1991). Collected and published by the owner's decision of 26 November 2026, also where a chain's terms or robots.txt say otherwise; collected politely (identified, rate-limited, never past a refusal or a challenge)

government-facts.name: Facts published by US government agencies, used by the owner's decision of 26 November 2026 even where the copy carries no licence or the site's own terms or robots.txt say otherwise (the Esri-hosted copy of the Social Security Administration's field office list, Recreation.gov's RIDB export, the California Health and Human Services open data portal; since 27 November 2026 also US cities', counties' and state transportation departments' open-data layers of accessible pedestrian signals and curb ramps, transit agencies' elevator lists, and Amtrak's station information, Amtrak being a federally chartered corporation owned by the United States). Federal works are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105) and facts are not protected by copyright in the United States (Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service, 499 U.S. 340, 1991); state agencies' facility lists are public records. Only facts are kept (names, positions, addresses, public telephone numbers, hours, accessibility), collected politely (identified, rate-limited, never past a refusal or a challenge)

directory-facts.name: Facts read from public listing pages: tourism boards' visitor listings (Simpleview), chambers of commerce's public member directories (ChamberMaster), businesses' own homepages, Yellow Pages lookups of businesses already in the packs, and (since 27 November 2026) museums' own accessibility pages (names, street addresses, positions, telephone numbers, websites, opening hours, categories, accessibility notes). The sites grant no licence; facts are not protected by copyright in the United States (Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service, 499 U.S. 340, 1991). Collected by the owner's decisions of 26 November 2026, politely (identified, rate-limited, never past a refusal, a challenge or a login); only facts are kept, never reviews, ratings, descriptions, photos, e-mail addresses or people's names, and one-person and home businesses are left out

accepted.name: Overture Maps Foundation places
accepted.attribution: Places data from the Overture Maps Foundation (overturemaps.org), under CDLA Permissive 2.0 (some of its sources under Apache 2.0); the licence text is in LICENSES/.
accepted.query: SELECT id AS key, names.primary AS name, {cls} AS cls, bbox.ymin AS lat, bbox.xmin AS lon, {brand} AS brand, {brand_qid} AS brand_qid, {phones} AS phones, {websites} AS websites FROM read_parquet('{src}', hive_partitioning = 1) WHERE bbox.xmin BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND bbox.ymin BETWEEN {south} AND {north} AND confidence >= 0.6 AND COALESCE(CAST({status} AS VARCHAR), '') <> 'permanently_closed'
accepted.history: From the first build on; earlier monthly releases are merged first (overture_seed_releases) while Overture still keeps them in its bucket. Keyed by the GERS id. The newest release is found from the bucket's list. A place Overture marks permanently closed is closed at its last month.
accepted.contact: The phone numbers and web sites Overture gives (phones, websites: the first of each, cleaned by placepacks/contact.py) are kept as each business's contact details. Its e-mail addresses and social-media accounts are never read.
accepted.notes: Overture renamed its category columns in 2026 ("categories" became "taxonomy" and "basic_category"): the build reads the release's columns first and uses taxonomy.primary, else basic_category, else the old categories.primary. Places whose operating_status is "permanently_closed" are left out of the month's data, so their earlier record stays, closed at the last build that listed them open.

accepted.name: Foursquare Open Source Places
accepted.attribution: Foursquare Open Source Places, Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc., under the Apache License 2.0 (NOTICE and licence text in LICENSES/).
accepted.query: SELECT fsq_place_id AS key, name, COALESCE(fsq_category_labels[1], '') AS cls, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon, CAST(date_created AS VARCHAR) AS first, CAST(date_closed AS VARCHAR) AS last, {tel} AS phone, {website} AS website FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE longitude BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND latitude BETWEEN {south} AND {north}
accepted.history: The dates Foursquare records: when a place was created and when it closed (date_closed), so closed businesses are kept closed. Keyed by fsq_place_id.
accepted.prepare_query: SELECT fsq_place_id, name, fsq_category_labels, latitude, longitude, date_created, date_closed, CAST({tel} AS VARCHAR) AS tel, CAST({website} AS VARCHAR) AS website FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE country IN ({countries})
accepted.contact: The phone number (tel) and web site (website) Foursquare gives are kept as each business's contact details, cleaned by placepacks/contact.py. Its email, facebook_id, instagram and twitter columns are never read.
accepted.local_query: SELECT fsq_place_id AS key, name, COALESCE(fsq_category_labels[1], '') AS cls, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon, CAST(date_created AS VARCHAR) AS first, CAST(date_closed AS VARCHAR) AS last, {tel} AS phone, {website} AS website FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE longitude BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND latitude BETWEEN {south} AND {north}
accepted.notes: Foursquare's official copy is the Hugging Face dataset foursquare/fsq-os-places (https://huggingface.co/datasets/foursquare/fsq-os-places), behind a free sign-in. The owner's Program Downloader copies each month's files, unchanged, into this repository's release "uploaded-sources" (fsq-<date>-<file>, fsq-<date>-NOTICE.txt and the manifest fsq-<date>.json). The prepare job reads the newest upload once, file by file, keeping only the covered countries (and PR, Puerto Rico, which Foursquare files as its own country) and the columns the build uses, and each region takes its box from that local copy. Until the first upload is there, the source is skipped (waiting for the owner's upload from Program Downloader).

The monthly file (about 1 GB zipped, 10 GB of CSV, about 9 million NPIs) is downloaded by the prepare job to the runner's larger disk, read once as a stream out of the zip, filtered at once to the storefront kinds of the taxonomy allowlist in sources.json (class_map, with each code's plain name in allowlist_names), written as a small CSV and the zip deleted; the CSV is split per state. Kept: pharmacies (not mail-order, institutional, long-term care or nuclear ones), clinics and urgent care, dialysis, surgery and imaging centres, dentists, optometrists and opticians, hearing aid shops and audiologists, physical therapy, chiropractors, clinical laboratories, medical supply and orthotics stores. Station telephone numbers, hours and directions are not kept. The API wants a key: the GitHub secret NREL_API_KEY (free from developer.nlr.gov/signup, emailed), else the public DEMO_KEY, which allows a few requests an hour per address and is enough for this one request a month unless the runner's address is busy. Terms (developer.nlr.gov/terms): the data may be used for any purpose whatsoever; the names DOE, NLR and the Alliance may not be used to endorse or promote, and the user indemnifies them. accepted.attribution: Parks, visitor centers, campgrounds and places from the National Park Service's Data API (developer.nps.gov), a work of the United States government (public domain); facts only.
accepted.history: From the first build that has the key on (the API has no opening dates); a place that leaves the API is closed at its last build.
accepted.contact: The first voice telephone number, the place's nps.gov page and its hours in OpenStreetMap's syntax, with the dated exceptions that have not ended (placepacks/hours.py, nps_hours: "Mo-Su 09:00-17:00; 2026 Nov 01-2027 Apr 30 off"). When the API's words for a day are not plain hours, the hours description is kept in the note instead. The TTY number is kept in the note ("TTY: ..."). Fax numbers and e-mail addresses are never read.
accepted.notes: About 470 park units, their visitor centers and campgrounds, and the places the parks describe (endpoints parks, visitorcenters, campgrounds and places; about 25 requests a month, 2 seconds apart, by the prepare job; placepacks/nps_api.py). The API needs a free key: the owner signs up at nps.gov/subjects/developer (the key arrives by e-mail) and stores it as the repository secret NPS_API_KEY, which only the prepare step reads; it is sent in the X-Api-Key header, never in the address, and never printed. Without the secret this source is skipped and the build goes on. A record with the same name as a point of nps-poi within 400 m is that point: the nps-poi point stays and takes these details (dedupe_carry), so a place is not listed twice. The note holds the TTY number, hours that could not be written in OpenStreetMap's syntax, campground accessibility (wheelchair access, ADA information, access roads, RV and trailer lengths), amenities and the number of reservable sites (data only, never spoken). Photos (often credited to others), long descriptions, e-mail addresses and anything with a credit line are never read.

accepted.name: Social Security field offices, with their address, telephone number and weekday hours
accepted.attribution: Social Security field offices from the Social Security Administration's office list, as published in an ArcGIS copy (SSA_Field_Offices) by Esri; facts of a United States government agency.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the list has no opening dates); an office that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.contact: The office's public telephone number and its weekday hours in OpenStreetMap's syntax ("Mo-Fr 09:00-16:00"; days with other hours written apart), from the list's MONDAY..FRIDAY_OPEN_TIME and _CLOSE_TIME (placepacks/hours.py, weekday_table). The address is the place's note ("Address: 68 Sewall St, Ste 209, Augusta, ME 04330"), which the "nearest Social Security office" lookup says.
accepted.notes: About 1,170 field offices, named "Social Security office, <city>", at the list's own points. ssa.gov refuses every program ("Access Denied", even for robots.txt), so this ArcGIS copy of SSA's own list, published by Esri's health GIS staff without a licence, is used by the owner's decision of 26 November 2026; no evasion of ssa.gov's block is ever tried. Read once a month by the prepare job (one or two requests, placepacks/ssa_offices.py) and split per state. Only the office code, name, address lines, city, state, ZIP code, telephone number and weekday opening and closing times are asked for: the layer's internal columns (costs, staff numbers, square feet, lease dates, waiting times, utilisation, local demographics, fax numbers) are never requested or stored.

accepted.short: US cities' and counties' open data
accepted.attribution: Public places from the open-data layers of US cities and counties (Socrata and ArcGIS portals found each month; the month's list of layers, with each publisher, is layers-city-facilities.json in this repository's release city-facilities), read by place-packs (placepacks/directories/city_facilities.py); facts of local governments.
accepted.history: From the first build that has a set, month by month, keyed by the layer and the record's own id. A state whose collection fails in a month keeps its places from the previous set (up to three months running); a layer that refuses or fails within a state's run is missing that month.
accepted.contact: The place's public telephone number, website and opening hours as the city gives them, cleaned by placepacks/contact.py (city-facilities counts as a government source); hours are turned into OpenStreetMap's syntax where placepacks/hours.py can be sure (one range a day, or a day field each), otherwise the city's own words become the note ("Hours: ..."). Only the mapped fields are ever requested: managers' or staff names and e-mail addresses are never read.
accepted.notes: Found and read automatically once a month by the city-facilities workflow (the 18th): a discovery job sweeps the Socrata catalogue (api.us.socrata.com) and ArcGIS Hub's search (hub.arcgis.com) for 14 keywords (facilities, community centers, recreation centers, libraries, city hall, municipal buildings, parks facilities, senior centers, points of interest ...), keeps US city and county layers of points with a name field (state, federal and university portals, private accounts and layers whose titles name inspections, permits, energy use, staff or the like are left out; a layer with people fields, such as first and last names or job titles, is a staff directory and is never read), maps their fields automatically (NAME/FACILITY/FAC_NAME, ADDRESS, CITY, ZIP, PHONE, HOURS or one field per weekday, TYPE, WEBSITE) and reads one record of each to find its state; placepacks/data/city_facilities_overrides.json adds, skips or corrects layers by hand. Then one job per state reads its layers (at most 5,000 records a layer; a bigger layer is not a list of public places and is left out whole). The kind of each place comes from its type field, else its name, else the layer's title. Owner's decisions: government data regardless of licence (26 November 2026); every US city and town that publishes facilities data, found automatically, with a manual override list (27 November 2026). Research of 27 November 2026: the catalogues answered without a key; samples (Chicago's senior centers, Seattle's community centers, Phoenix's park buildings, Harris County's community centers) mapped name, address, phone, hours and type correctly. Until the first set is there, the source is skipped.

accepted.name: Campus and indoor maps: buildings, accessible entrances, elevators, accessible parking and restrooms, routes, desks and dining of colleges, hospitals, zoos and other sites (MazeMap, universities' campus GIS layers; Concept3D waiting for the owner's decision)
accepted.attribution: Buildings and accessibility features from the organisations' own campus and indoor maps (MazeMap) and universities' open campus GIS layers (ArcGIS Hub), read by place-packs (placepacks/mapvendors); the month's list of maps, with each organisation, is map-vendors-orgs.json in this repository's release map-vendors.
accepted.history: No history: the site features of the newest monthly set (the site_features table is written whole each build). A unit whose collection fails or is blocked keeps the previous set's file (up to three months).
accepted.contact: A site's own website (its homepage from the discovery) where its place lacks one; the site's note ("Indoor map with wheelchair routes").
accepted.notes: Owner's decisions of 27 November 2026 (queue item Q2): plot each building of a campus with its accessible entrances; use campus map platforms with public data and universities' open GIS layers; scraping campus websites approved where needed, with the standing limits (facts only; no people's names; polite, identified, rate-limited; never past a CAPTCHA, a login or an anti-bot challenge, no headless or Chrome-imitating browser, no other IP address: a refusal is recorded as blocked). Discovery (placepacks/mapvendors/discover.py, monthly, in shards) scans the homepages of every active IPEDS institution and of Wikidata's US hospitals, zoos, aquariums, museums, convention centres, stadiums, malls and airports, and up to three of each one's own map, visitor, parking and accessibility pages, for the fingerprints of the vendors in placepacks/mapvendors/registry.py (robots.txt obeyed); unknown map embeds go to new-map-vendors.txt. Collectors: MazeMap (public API without a key; rooms and offices never read, only POI types that name a kind: entrances, elevators, toilets, parking, desks, dining), universities' ArcGIS building layers (name, address; layers with people fields never read), Concept3D (ready, but api.concept3d.com's robots.txt disallows all programs, so it records "blocked" and reads nothing until the owner decides). Site rows are tied to the place already in the pack (its NCES or Wikidata key, else the same name nearby, else the campus area holding it).

Insurers' directories: only Location records (never Practitioner or PractitionerRole); a Location named like a person or a practitioner's own office, without a position, named only by its street address, or saying nothing about accessibility or hours is left out; robots.txt obeyed. Hospitals' pages: the hospitals of Wikidata with an official website; the homepage and up to three of its own accessibility, interpreter and patients-and-visitors pages; only a fixed list of facts is kept (never the page's text), and the phone number of a sentence about accessibility services. Rows are tied to the clinic or hospital already in the pack by the NPI (cms-nppes-organisations), the Wikidata key, or the same name within 400 m; a row that matches nothing adds nothing. accepted.attribution: Stores and amenities of US malls and outlet centres from the malls' own websites (Tanger, Macerich, Brookfield Properties, Westfield, CBL Properties and independent malls), read by place-packs (placepacks/indoor/malls.py); facts only.

accepted.notes: Owner's decisions of 27 November 2026 (notes/helper-rules.txt, queue item Q3): scraping mall and airport websites approved, stopping at any block; the standing limits: facts only (store names, category, floor or level, unit, hours, phone, website, gates, desks, restrooms, accessibility features); no people's names, no e-mail addresses, no descriptions, reviews, ratings or photos; polite, identified (User-Agent place-packs-indoor-directories), at least 2 seconds between requests to a host, a request budget per unit, robots.txt read first and obeyed; never past a CAPTCHA, a login or an anti-bot challenge, no headless or Chrome-imitating browser, no other IP address: a refusal is recorded as blocked and the site left. Collected once a month by the malls workflow (the 5th), one job per operator (placepacks/indoor/malls.py): Tanger (tanger.com's sitemap; each centre's page data: stores with categories, suite and own hours, the centre's phone and weekly hours, its visitor-info amenities), Macerich (macerich.com's sitemap to each mall's own site; its Directory page: stores with level, phone and category, the mall's regular hours; its Services page), Brookfield Properties (its property sitemap to each mall's own site; the directory page's JSON: stores with phone, website, categories, level and the anchor store they are near, the mall's weekly hours; the visit page's questions and answers for amenities), Westfield US centres (the US sitemap; the retailers and restaurants pages' data: stores with categories, level and own hours, the centre's position and phone; the services cards), CBL Properties (its portfolio to each mall's own site; the directory's store names, the mall's phone and the coming week's hours), and three shares of every other mall with a website in Wikidata or OpenStreetMap (schema.org data, directory store links, the amenities the visitor pages name). Checked 27 November 2026 with one to three requests per site: Simon answers 403 and its robots.txt forbids automated collection; PREIT's property pages answer 403; Washington Prime's site has a TLS certificate that does not verify; Federal Realty's and Kimco's centre lists are script-only applications. Those five are recorded as not read and checked once a month. Mappedin maps (Macerich, Brookfield, Tanger) need a customer key and are not read. A mall gets the position and place key of the Wikidata or OpenStreetMap mall with the same website host, else the same name; stores and amenities take the mall's position, with the level, unit and "near" anchor store in the note. An amenity a mall's questions and answers deny ("No, ...") is left out.

accepted.attribution: Gates, shops, restaurants, restrooms, desks and accessibility services of US airports from the airports' own websites and their public Atrius (LocusLabs) maps, read by place-packs (placepacks/indoor/airports.py, placepacks/mapvendors/atrius.py); airports from OurAirports (public domain); facts only.

accepted.attribution: Registered Retail Dealers of Cigarettes, Tobacco and Vapor Products of the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance (data.ny.gov, dataset 55xf-9jat); trade names and positions only.
accepted.history: From the first build on; a dealer that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 22,700 registered retailers (convenience stores, petrol stations, smoke and vape shops), New York City included, with the portal's points. The privacy rule keeps the DBA name, else the legal name only when it is a company's (Inc, LLC, Corp ...): a retailer listed under a person's name (the column is 'last name or business name') is left out.

queries.select: cor_id || '-' || cor_seq_nmbr AS key, case(dba_name IS NOT NULL, dba_name, true, last_or_bus_name) AS name, georeference AS point
queries.where: georeference IS NOT NULL AND (dba_name IS NOT NULL OR (upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% INC%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% LLC%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%L.L.C%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% CORP%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%COMPANY%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% CO.%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% CO' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% LTD%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% LP' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% L.P.%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% LLP%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%PLLC%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%PARTNERS%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% TRUST%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% GROUP%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%ENTERPRISE%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%HOLDINGS%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%ASSOCIATION%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '% CLUB%' OR upper(last_or_bus_name) LIKE '%CHURCH%'))

accepted.name: New York State DMV-licensed repair shops, inspection stations and dealers
accepted.short: the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles
accepted.attribution: Facilities Licensed by the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (data.ny.gov, dataset nhjr-rpi2); facility names, positions and licence dates only.
accepted.history: Each facility from its first licence (original issuance, often decades back) to its expiry; keyed by the facility number, so a renamed facility keeps its old name with its dates.
accepted.notes: Repair shops, inspection stations and new and used car dealers (business types RS, RSB, ISP, DLN, DLU); wholesalers, dismantlers, scrap processors and the like are left out. Only the facility name is kept; the owner's name is never downloaded, and a facility named exactly as its owner is left out inside the portal's query.

queries.select: facility AS key, facility_name, facility_name_overflow, business_type AS kind, georeference AS point, origional_issuance_date AS first, expiration_date AS last
queries.where: georeference IS NOT NULL AND facility_name IS NOT NULL AND business_type IN ('RS', 'RSB', 'ISP', 'DLN', 'DLU') AND (owner_name IS NULL OR upper(facility_name) != upper(owner_name))

accepted.name: New York State salons, nail salons and barber shops (licensed businesses)
accepted.short: the New York State Department of State
accepted.attribution: Appearance Enhancement and Barber Business Licensees of the New York State Department of State (data.ny.gov, dataset y3u4-jbgh); business names, positions and licence dates only.
accepted.history: Each business licence from its issue date to its expiry; keyed by the licence number.
accepted.notes: About 27,600 appearance enhancement businesses (hair, nail, skin and waxing salons) and barber shops with the portal's points; area renters (individuals renting a chair) and post office box addresses are left out. Privacy rule (owner_column): the licence holder's name is read only to compare, and a business whose name is the holder's own name ('Oscar E Garcia Torres' of 'Garcia Oscar Enriques') is left out.

queries.select: license_number AS key, business_name AS name, license_holder_name AS holder, georeference AS point, license_issue_date AS first, license_expiration_date AS last
queries.where: license_type IN ('DOSAEBUSINESS', 'DOSBARSHOPOWNER') AND georeference IS NOT NULL AND business_name IS NOT NULL AND NOT upper(coalesce(business_address_1, '') || ' ' || coalesce(business_address_2, '')) LIKE '%BOX %'

accepted.name: New York State licensed adult-use cannabis shops
accepted.short: the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
accepted.attribution: Registered Retail Dealers of Adult-use Cannabis of the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance (data.ny.gov, dataset gttd-5u6y); company names and positions only.
accepted.history: From the first build on; a shop that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 700 licensed cannabis shops with the portal's points. The dataset has only the licensee's legal name, so only names that are clearly a company's (Inc, LLC, Corp, Ltd ...) are kept.

queries.select: ocm_license_number AS key, legal_name AS name, georeference AS point
queries.where: georeference IS NOT NULL AND (upper(legal_name) LIKE '% INC%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% LLC%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%L.L.C%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% CORP%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%COMPANY%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% CO.%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% CO' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% LTD%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% LP' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% L.P.%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% LLP%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%PLLC%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%PARTNERS%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% TRUST%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% GROUP%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%ENTERPRISE%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%HOLDINGS%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%ASSOCIATION%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '% CLUB%' OR upper(legal_name) LIKE '%CHURCH%')

accepted.name: New York State WIC grocers and pharmacies (located by address)

accepted.history: From the first build on; a store that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 2,900 grocers and pharmacies that accept WIC, located by the offline geocoder against the NAD (the dataset has addresses only). Store names only; the dataset has no owner names.

queries.select: facility_name AS name, type AS kind, street_address AS street, city, zip
queries.where: facility_name IS NOT NULL AND street_address IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: Connecticut state licences of premises (liquor permits, bakeries, pharmacies, petrol stations ...)
accepted.short: the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection
accepted.attribution: State Licenses and Credentials of the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection and Department of Administrative Services (data.ct.gov, dataset ngch-56tr), public domain; business names, located points and licence dates only.
accepted.history: Each credential from its issue date to its expiry; an inactive one (lapsed, cancelled) ends at its expiry. Keyed by the credential id.
accepted.notes: About 45,000 premises credentials since the 1990s (about 15,000 active): restaurant, café, tavern, club, hotel, package store and grocery liquor permits, brew pubs and farm wineries, bakeries, dairy stores, frozen dessert shops, pharmacies, petrol stations, vape shops, health clubs, opticians and funeral homes, located by the offline geocoder against the NAD. Cottage food operations (home kitchens), brand labels, temporary and out-of-state permits and every individual credential (nurses, electricians ...) are left out. Privacy rule: the DBA name, else the business name; a credential held by an individual or sole proprietor is kept only under a DBA different from the holder's name (that comparison is made inside the portal's query, so the holder's name is never downloaded).

queries.select: credentialid AS key, case(dba IS NOT NULL, dba, true, businessname) AS name, credential AS kind, address AS street, city, zip, issuedate AS first, expirationdate AS last, case(active = '1', '', true, 'yes') AS closed
queries.where: credential IN ('RESTAURANT LIQUOR', 'RESTAURANT WINE & BEER', 'RESTAURANT BEER', 'CAFE LIQUOR', 'CONNECTICUT CRAFT CAFE LIQUOR', 'CAFE WINE-BEER-CIDER', 'TAVERN LIQUOR', 'CLUB LIQUOR', 'NON PROFIT CLUB LIQUOR', 'PACKAGE STORE LIQUOR', 'GROCERY BEER', 'DRUGGIST LIQUOR', 'BREW PUB LIQUOR', 'MANUFACTURER FOR BEER AND BREW PUB', 'MANUFACTURER BEER', 'FARM BREWERY LIQUOR', 'FARM WINERY LIQUOR', 'FARM DISTILLERY LIQUOR', 'BOWLING ESTABLISHMENT LIQUOR', 'BOWLING ESTABLISHMENT BEER AND WINE', 'NON PROFIT THEATER LIQUOR', 'COLISEUM LIQUOR', 'GOLF COUNTRY CLUB LIQUOR', 'BAKERY', 'RETAIL DAIRY STORE', 'FROZEN DESSERT RETAILER', 'PHARMACY', 'RETAIL GASOLINE DEALER', 'DEALER OF ELECTRONIC NICOTINE DELIVERY SYSTEM OR VAPOR PRODUCT', 'HEALTH CLUB', 'Funeral Home', 'Optical Selling Permit', 'HOTEL LIQUOR', 'HOTEL LIQUOR (50000 or less population)', 'HOTEL LIQUOR (50000 or more population)', 'HOTEL LIQUOR (10000 or less population)') AND issuedate IS NOT NULL AND address IS NOT NULL AND state = 'CT' AND (dba IS NOT NULL OR businessname IS NOT NULL) AND (type NOT IN ('INDIVIDUAL', 'SOLE PROPRIETOR', 'EMPLOYEE ONLY') OR (dba IS NOT NULL AND upper(dba) != upper(name)))

accepted.name: Connecticut licensed car dealers and repairers
accepted.short: the Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles
accepted.attribution: Licensed Automobile Dealers, Repairers, Leasing Companies of the Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles (data.ct.gov, dataset apne-w8c6), public domain; business names and positions only.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the dataset has only expiry dates); a licence that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 4,600 new and used car dealers and general repairers in Connecticut with the portal's points; leasing companies, recyclers and out-of-state licensees are left out. Only the business name is read (the dataset has no owner names); names that look like 'Surname, Given' are left out.

queries.select: license_num AS key, business_name AS name, license_type AS kind, geocoded_column AS point
queries.where: state = 'CT' AND geocoded_column IS NOT NULL AND business_name IS NOT NULL AND license_type IN ('NEW DEALER', 'USED DEALER', 'GENERAL REPAIRER')

accepted.name: Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish registered businesses
accepted.short: the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge
accepted.attribution: Businesses Registered with EBR Parish, City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge Finance Department (data.brla.gov, dataset xw6s-bcqm), public domain; trade names, positions and dates only.
accepted.history: Each business location from its opening date to its closing date (a closed account ends there); keyed by the account and location numbers.
accepted.notes: Storefront businesses inside East Baton Rouge Parish by NAICS code, as for San Francisco (restaurants, bars, shops, petrol stations, garages, salons, hotels ...); accounts outside the parish or outside Louisiana are left out. Only the trade name (tname) is kept; the contact person, mailing address and legal name are never downloaded. Privacy rule: a sole proprietor (or an account without an ownership type) is kept only under a trade name different from its legal name (compared inside the portal's query).

queries.select: taccount || '-' || tacctlocation AS key, tname AS name, tnaic AS naics, geolocation AS point, topendate AS first, tclosedate AS last, case(tstatus = 'C', 'yes', true, '') AS closed
queries.where: location NOT IN ('Outside Louisiana', 'Outside EBR Parish') AND tname IS NOT NULL AND tnaic IS NOT NULL AND geolocation IS NOT NULL AND ((townership IS NOT NULL AND townership != 'Sole Proprietor') OR upper(tname) != upper(tlegalname))

accepted.name: San Diego County food facility permits (located by address)
accepted.short: the County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality
accepted.attribution: Food Facility Permits of the County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality (data.sandiegocounty.gov, dataset c5ez-ufrd), public domain; facility names and located points only.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the dataset has no opening dates); a permit that leaves the list is closed at its last build. Keyed by the record id.
accepted.notes: About 12,000 active restaurants, markets and food shops of San Diego County, located by the offline geocoder against the NAD (the portal's latitude and longitude are empty). Mobile food units, carts, home kitchens (microenterprise home kitchens), caterers, school and health care kitchens and vending machines are left out. Only the facility name; the permit owner's name, phone and e-mail are never downloaded.

queries.select: record_id AS key, record_name AS name, business_type AS kind, address AS street, city, zip
queries.where: active_permit = 'A' AND record_name IS NOT NULL AND address IS NOT NULL AND business_type IN ('Restaurant Food Facility', 'Pre-Packaged Retail Market', 'Retail Market with Deli', 'Retail Food Processing')

accepted.name: New Orleans active occupational (business) licences
accepted.attribution: Active Occupational Licenses of the City of New Orleans (data.nola.gov, dataset iqay-p646), CC0; business names, positions and start dates only.
accepted.history: Each business from its start date; one that leaves the list of active licences is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: Storefront business types only (restaurants, bars, hotels, shops, salons, petrol stations, garages, laundries, gyms, museums ...): home-based offices, street artists and event vendors, taxis, contractors, bed and breakfasts and short-term rentals are left out by type. Only the business name; the phone is never downloaded, and the owner's name is read only to compare (owner_column): a business named as a person-owner's own name is left out. This dataset states CC0; the older occupational licence dataset (hjcd-grvu) states no licence and is still not used.

queries.select: businesslicensenumber AS key, businessname AS name, ownername AS owner, businesstype AS kind, the_geom AS point, businessstartdate AS first
queries.where: the_geom IS NOT NULL AND businessname IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: New Orleans alcohol beverage outlets
accepted.attribution: Alcohol Beverage Outlets of the City of New Orleans (data.nola.gov, dataset qfg2-kjjz), CC0; business names and positions only.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the dataset has no dates); an outlet that leaves the list is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 1,500 restaurants, bars, hotels, stores and venues licensed to sell alcohol; caterers, wholesalers and food service contractors are left out. Only the business name (the part after 'dba' when the name holds both); the owner's name is read only to compare (owner_column).

queries.select: objectid AS key, businessname AS name, ownername AS owner, businesstype AS kind, the_geom AS point
queries.where: the_geom IS NOT NULL AND businessname IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: Baltimore City liquor licences (2002 to now, located by address range)
accepted.short: the Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City
accepted.attribution: Liquor licences of the Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City (Baltimore City CityView licences table), Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported; trade names, located points and licence dates only.
accepted.history: Each licence from its first licence year to its last (yearly records since 2002), one record per licence and trade name; a licence renewed within the last year is open.
accepted.notes: About 30,000 licence-years of taverns, restaurants, package goods stores, hotels, clubs, breweries and venues. Maryland is left out of the National Address Database, so the addresses are placed along the street's TIGER/Line address range (matched by street name, number and ZIP code): about where the house number falls, not an exact point. Only the trade name; the licensees' first and last names are never downloaded. The City's points layers of current licensees state no licence and are not used.

fetch.where: TradeName IS NOT NULL AND AddrStreet IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: Sacramento County business licences (commercial premises, located by address)
accepted.attribution: Business Licenses of the County of Sacramento (Sacramento County GIS open data), under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; business names, located points and licence dates only.
accepted.history: Each licence from its filing date to its expiry; keyed by the record number.
accepted.notes: Licences of the unincorporated county at commercial premises only (the county's own 'Commercial' location flag): home-based businesses are left out, and only storefront activities (restaurants, shops, salons, garages, car dealers, petrol stations, gyms, laundries, storage) are kept. Located by the offline geocoder against the NAD (the layer's own points are not usable). Only the business name; the phone is never downloaded. The layer's text says public domain dedication and its tag says CC BY 4.0: it is credited under CC BY 4.0, the owner's choice.

fetch.where: Location = 'Commercial' AND Business_Name IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: Wake County, North Carolina restaurants and food places
accepted.attribution: Restaurants in Wake County, Wake County Department of Environmental Services (Wake County GIS open data), CC BY 4.0; names, positions and opening dates only.
accepted.history: Each restaurant from its opening date (back to the 1980s); one that leaves the layer is closed at its last build. Keyed by the state facility id (HSISID).
accepted.notes: About 3,000 restaurants, food stands, limited food services and meat markets of Raleigh and Wake County; mobile food units, push carts, school, institutional and elderly nutrition kitchens are left out. Names only; phones are never downloaded.

fetch.where: FACILITYTYPE IN ('1 - Restaurant', '2 - Food Stands', '14 - Limited Food', '30 - Meat Market')

accepted.name: Cambridge, Massachusetts food establishment and tobacco permits
accepted.attribution: Food Establishment Permits (data.cambridgema.gov, dataset iect-ma2e) and Tobacco Licenses (dataset ryaf-48sr) of the City of Cambridge, Open Data Commons PDDL; business names, positions and permit dates only.
accepted.history: Each place from its first permit (2016 on) to its latest, one record per address and name; a permit issued within the last 13 months is open.
accepted.notes: Restaurants, cafés, bars, food shops, bakeries and tobacco shops (yearly permits). Only the DBA name, else the business name when it is a company's; the applicant's name is never downloaded. Daycare, institution and wholesale kitchens are left out.

queries.select: full_address AS key, case(dba IS NOT NULL, dba, true, business_name) AS name, food_est_permit_type AS kind, coordinates AS point, issue_date AS first, issue_date AS last
queries.where: permit_type = 'Food Establishment' AND coordinates IS NOT NULL AND issue_date IS NOT NULL AND (dba IS NOT NULL OR (upper(business_name) LIKE '% INC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LLC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%L.L.C%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CORP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%COMPANY%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CO.%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CO' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LTD%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LP' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% L.P.%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LLP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%PLLC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%PARTNERS%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% TRUST%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% GROUP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%ENTERPRISE%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%HOLDINGS%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%ASSOCIATION%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CLUB%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%CHURCH%'))

queries.select: full_address AS key, case(dba IS NOT NULL, dba, true, business_name) AS name, 'Tobacco' AS kind, coordinates AS point, issue_date AS first, issue_date AS last
queries.where: coordinates IS NOT NULL AND issue_date IS NOT NULL AND (dba IS NOT NULL OR (upper(business_name) LIKE '% INC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LLC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%L.L.C%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CORP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%COMPANY%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CO.%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CO' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LTD%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LP' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% L.P.%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% LLP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%PLLC%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%PARTNERS%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% TRUST%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% GROUP%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%ENTERPRISE%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%HOLDINGS%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%ASSOCIATION%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '% CLUB%' OR upper(business_name) LIKE '%CHURCH%'))

accepted.name: Washington, DC liquor licences (ABCA)
accepted.short: the District of Columbia Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration
accepted.attribution: ABCA Liquor License Locations of the District of Columbia Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration (opendata.dc.gov), CC BY 4.0; trade names, positions and expiry dates only.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the layer has expiry dates only); a retired licence ends at its expiry. Keyed by the licence number.
accepted.notes: Restaurants, taverns, nightclubs, hotels, clubs, liquor stores, groceries and venues licensed to sell alcohol, under their trade names; delivery services, caterers, wholesalers, manufacturers, railroads, vessels, internet sellers and bed and breakfasts are left out. The applicant (owner) is never downloaded.

accepted.name: Sioux Falls, South Dakota alcohol licences
accepted.attribution: Alcohol and Video Lottery Licensing of the City of Sioux Falls (Sioux Falls GIS open data), CC BY 4.0; business names and positions only.
accepted.history: From the first build on (the layer has no dates); a licence that leaves the layer is closed at its last build.
accepted.notes: About 1,000 active on-sale and off-sale alcohol licences (bars, restaurants, liquor and convenience stores) with the city's points; South Dakota is not in the NAD, but this layer has its own points. Only the business name; the owner's name is read only to compare (owner_column).

fetch.where: Status = 'Active' AND BusinessName IS NOT NULL

accepted.name: Arlington (Texas) food establishments (inspections)
accepted.attribution: Food establishment inspections of the City of Arlington, Texas (Arlington open data), CC BY 4.0; names, positions and inspection dates only.
accepted.history: Each establishment from its first to its last inspection in the layer, one record per name and address; one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open.
accepted.notes: Restaurants, fast food, bars, delis, bakeries, groceries and convenience stores; schools, hospital and retirement kitchens, caterers, warehouses and seasonal stands are left out. No scores are kept.

accepted.name: NLS braille and talking-book libraries (Library of Congress network)
accepted.short: the Library of Congress National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled
accepted.attribution: Braille and talking-book libraries from the Library of Congress National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS), "Find Your Library" (loc.gov/nls/find-your-library/), a work of the United States government (public domain); located by their addresses.
accepted.history: From the first build on (a place dropped from the source is closed at its last build).
accepted.notes: About 90 regional and subregional libraries and outreach centers of the NLS network, where blind and print-disabled readers borrow braille, talking books and players. One web page, read once a month by the prepare job (robots.txt allows it; one request), turned into names and street addresses (placepacks.fetch.nls_to_csv) and placed by the offline geocoder. A library listed only by a post office box, and the overseas entry, cannot be placed and are left out. The librarians' names, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses and the counties served are never read.

accepted.name: Medicare medical equipment suppliers (pharmacies, medical supply, opticians, orthotics and prosthetics)
accepted.short: the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
accepted.attribution: Medical Equipment Suppliers of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (data.cms.gov Provider Data, dataset ct36-nrcq), a work of the United States government (public domain); business names, positions and participation dates only.
accepted.history: Each supplier from the date it began to participate in Medicare (participationbegindate); one that leaves the list is closed at its last build. Keyed by CMS's supplier id.
accepted.notes: About 56,800 suppliers of medical equipment to Medicare patients with CMS's own positions: retail pharmacies (the only open federal pharmacy list with coordinates), medical supply and oxygen companies, opticians and optometrists' shops, orthotics and prosthetics, hearing aid shops. Read for each state from CMS's Provider Data API (pages of 1,500). Organisations only: a supplier whose provider type is an individual practitioner (physician, nurse practitioner, independent therapist, dentist) is left out, and so is a name that looks like a person's ("Surname, Given", a doctor's title or a credential such as MD, OD or DPM at the end). The location's own trade name is used (practicename), else the legal name; store numbers and Inc/LLC are removed. Telephone numbers are never read. The same pharmacies are often in cms-nppes-organisations too; a lookup gives a place listed by both once.

accepted.name: Bureau of Land Management recreation sites (campgrounds, trailheads, visitor centers, boat launches)
accepted.attribution: BLM National Recreation Site Points of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM national ArcGIS hub), a work of the United States government (public domain).

fetch.where: FET_SUBTYPE IN ('Campground', 'Trail Head', 'Access Point', 'Staging Area', 'Point of Interest', 'Interpretive Site', 'Scenic Overlook', 'Picnic Area', 'Day Use Site', 'Group Shelter', 'Boat Launch', 'Boat Ramp', 'Boat Takeout', 'Boat Dock', 'Water Access', 'Rapid', 'Visitor Center', 'BLM Ranger Station/Field Office/Contact Station', 'OHV Designated Area', 'Natural Area/Endangered Area', 'Cabin', 'Cabin - Reservable - Fee', 'Cabin - Non Reservable - No Fee', 'Lighthouse', 'Fire Lookout', 'Cave Entry Point', 'Rock Climbing')

accepted.history: From the first build on (a place dropped from the source is closed at its last build).
accepted.notes: About 5,000 named recreation places on public lands managed by the BLM: campgrounds, trailheads, visitor centers and ranger stations, boat launches, picnic areas, overlooks, interpretive sites, cabins, named river rapids and points of interest. Individual campsites, toilets, parking areas, river miles, water taps, horse corrals and management-area markers (about 5,000 rows) are left out, and so are names that only say what the thing is ("Toilet"). The layer's licence text is BLM's standard "provided as is" disclaimer; the data is a work of the United States government.

accepted.name: Bureau of Land Management accessible recreation sites, with their accessibility descriptions
accepted.attribution: BLM National Accessible Recreation Points of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM national ArcGIS hub), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on (a place dropped from the source is closed at its last build).
accepted.notes: About 165 BLM recreation sites with full accessibility descriptions (accessible toilets, paths and their slopes, parking, fishing piers). The description is kept as the place's note (FORMAT.md, "Notes on places": data for programs, never spoken by a lookup), cut to about 1,200 characters, with any e-mail address or telephone number taken out. The layer's telephone and e-mail columns are never read.

accepted.name: Bureau of Reclamation recreation sites (campgrounds, day-use areas and cabin areas at its reservoirs)
accepted.attribution: Reclamation Recreation Sites of the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation_Public, ArcGIS Online), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on (a place dropped from the source is closed at its last build).
accepted.notes: About 1,300 campgrounds, day-use areas and cabin areas at Reclamation's lakes and reservoirs, as areas (their outlines, simplified to about 20 m), so a picture taken inside one is "at" it. The licence text is Reclamation's "as is" disclaimer; the data is a work of the United States government.

accepted.name: Tennessee Valley Authority recreation sites (boat ramps, campgrounds, marinas, stream access)
accepted.attribution: TVA Recreation Points of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA-GIS, ArcGIS Online), made publicly available by TVA Natural Resources; a work of the United States government (public domain).

fetch.where: ASSET_TYPE IN ('Boat Ramp', 'Campground', 'Campgrounds', 'Marina', 'Stream Access Sites', 'Overlooks', 'Day Use Area', 'TVA Visitor Centers')

accepted.history: From the first build on (a place dropped from the source is closed at its last build).

accepted.name: Street and transit accessibility: accessible pedestrian signals from US cities' and transportation departments' open data, transit station elevators and escalators (MTA New York City Transit, MBTA) and Amtrak stations' accessibility and staffed hours (site features)
accepted.short: US cities' and transportation departments' open data, transit agencies and Amtrak
accepted.attribution: Accessible pedestrian signals from the open-data layers of US cities, counties and state transportation departments (found each month; the month's list of layers, with each publisher, is layers-street-access.json in this repository's release street-access); station elevators and escalators from MTA New York City Transit's and the MBTA's public lists; Amtrak station accessibility from Amtrak's Great American Stations; read by place-packs (placepacks/street_access).
accepted.history: No history: the site features of the newest monthly set (the site_features table is written whole each build); each signal's install date is in its note. A unit whose collection fails or is blocked keeps the previous set's file (up to three months).
accepted.contact: An Amtrak station's waiting-room hours (OpenStreetMap syntax) where its place (ntad-amtrak) lacks them; its note lists the accessibility facts and the ticket office's and passenger assistance's hours ("Accessibility (Amtrak station information): accessible platform; accessible restrooms; high platform; wheelchair available; no wheelchair lift; elevator; ticket office Mo-Su 05:00-23:30; passenger assistance Mo-Su 05:30-23:30").
accepted.notes: Owner's request of 27 November 2026 (notes/helper-rules.txt, queue item Q4); government data used regardless of a copy's licence (owner's decision of 26 November 2026); the standing limits: facts only; no people's names (a name added to an intersection's description is taken out), no e-mail addresses, no free-text comments; polite and identified (User-Agent place-packs-street-access), at least 3 seconds between requests to one host (10 for Great American Stations, its robots.txt Crawl-delay), a request budget per unit, robots.txt read and obeyed for websites; never past a CAPTCHA, a login or an anti-bot challenge, no headless or Chrome-imitating browser, no other IP address: a refusal is recorded as blocked and left. Units of the monthly street-access workflow (the 12th): signals (layers found in the Socrata catalogue and ArcGIS Hub by the words accessible pedestrian signal, audible signal, APS, pedestrian push button; a publisher must be a US government: a city, county, town, state or city transportation or public works department, a regional planning body; never a university, a company, a consultant's or a person's own account; positions checked to lie in a US state; fields mapped automatically: the intersection's name or its two streets, the install date, the status, locator tone, vibrating arrow, push button, speech message and an APS yes/no column; rows marked planned, pending, removed or without an APS left out); curb-ramps-1..4 (found the same way, for the navigation part only); mta-elevators (New York City Transit's elevator and escalator list, api-endpoint.mta.info nyct_ene_equipments.json, placed by the MTA station list on data.ny.gov, dataset 39hk-dx4f: each elevator and escalator with what it serves and whether it is ADA accessible; inactive equipment and other operators' left out); mbta-elevators (the MBTA's V3 API /facilities, without a key, at most 20 requests a minute); amtrak-stations (Great American Stations' station pages, about 530: the Accessibility list, the station building's elevator and the waiting room's, ticket office's and passenger assistance's hours; the station's position from the BTS layer ntad-amtrak; the regional contact's name and e-mail, the history and the ridership never read; Amtrak is a federally chartered corporation owned by the United States). A first check on 27 November 2026 (about 60 requests): the sweep found accessible pedestrian signal layers of New York City (4,546 signals with install dates), Seattle (456 in service), Charlotte, Atlanta, New Orleans, Ann Arbor and the Utah DOT (two layers), and about 30 curb ramp layers (New York City's pedestrian ramps, Austin, Tacoma, Portland, Sioux Falls, Anne Arundel County, Lake County IL, the Alaska, Colorado, Utah and Virginia DOTs, Washington DC ...); MTA: 370 elevators and 226 escalators in 143 stations; MBTA: 252 elevators and 169 escalators; Great American Stations answered (three stations read).

accepted.name: Accessible pedestrian signals and curb ramps from US cities' and transportation departments' open data, for the navigation part
accepted.short: US cities' and transportation departments' open data
accepted.attribution: Accessible pedestrian signals and curb ramps from the open-data layers of US cities, counties and state transportation departments (found each month; the month's list of layers, with each publisher, is layers-street-access.json in this repository's release street-access), read by place-packs (placepacks/street_access/open_data.py).
accepted.history: No history: the signals and curb ramps of the newest monthly set (the navigation part is rebuilt whole each time); each signal's install date and each ramp's year built are in its tags.
accepted.notes: The same monthly set as street-access, read again for the navigation part's nav_features (kinds "accessible pedestrian signal" and "curb ramp"; tags installed, locator_tone, vibration, button, speech, type, status; compliant, detectable_warning, condition; source: the publisher). Navigator.crossing_here says a listed signal within 35 m of a crossing ("The city lists an accessible pedestrian signal here (installed 2023-12-16)") and the listed curb ramps within 20 m. Curb ramps are only here, not in the extra part: a big city lists 100,000 or more, too many for the default download. Cities' sidewalk layers are not read: OpenStreetMap's sidewalks are already in the navigation part (footway=sidewalk ways with their surface, width and incline), and a city's every sidewalk as lines would about double the part's size without joining its routing graph.

accepted.name: Transit stations' entrances, elevators, escalators and stairs (GTFS pathways and levels) and stops' wheelchair boarding, from the open GTFS feeds (site features)
accepted.attribution: Station entrances, elevators, escalators and stairs, and stops' wheelchair boarding, from the agencies' GTFS feeds listed in the pack, each under its own open licence, found through the Mobility Database (mobilitydatabase.org).
accepted.history: No history: the stations as the feeds describe them at the build.
accepted.notes: Queue item Q4 (placepacks/readers/gtfs_stations.py). From the same feed files as the source gtfs: stops.txt's station entrances (location_type 2; kind accessible entrance when wheelchair_boarding is 1, its parent station's value when it says 0), levels.txt's level names, and pathways.txt's stairs (with stair_count), escalators and elevators, each once per pair of points, at its end's position or its station's; each tied to its station (site: the station's key in the extra part). Every stop and station whose wheelchair_boarding (or its station's) says yes or no gets the note "Wheelchair boarding: yes (the agency's timetable data)". The navigation part's gtfs-navigation reader adds the same entrances, elevators, escalators and stairs as navigation features. A feed without pathways.txt gives no station features (many bus-only feeds).

accepted.history: No places of its own: notes and site features for museums other sources list (imls-museums, wikidata), from the newest monthly set. A share whose collection fails keeps the previous set's file (up to three months).
accepted.contact: The note lists the facts found ("Accessibility (museum's website): audio description; touch tours; braille; large print; sign language; wheelchairs available; service animals welcome; sensory-friendly programs; page https://..."); no phone or hours are taken.
accepted.notes: Owner's request of 27 November 2026 (notes/helper-rules.txt, queue item Q4). The museums: the IMLS Museum Universe Data File's museums with a website (historical societies left out, as in imls-museums) and Wikidata's US museums with an official website, each website once (about 9,000), in eight shares of the monthly museum-access workflow (the 20th). For each: robots.txt first (obeyed), the homepage and up to two of its own accessibility, access-programs, sensory or visiting pages; only a fixed list of facts is kept (never the page's text), and for the accessible entrance the one sentence that says where it is (telephone numbers and e-mail addresses taken out). Polite and identified (User-Agent place-packs-museum-access), at least 2 seconds between requests to one host, never past a CAPTCHA, a login or an anti-bot challenge, no headless or Chrome-imitating browser, no other IP address: a museum whose site refuses is counted as blocked and left. A first check on 27 November 2026 (six museums): the Mobile Museum of Art, the Museum of Fine Arts Boston and the Perot Museum answered (facts found); the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Art Institute of Chicago and the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History answered 403 (blocked, never got round). Rows are tied to the museum already in the pack by its IMLS or Wikidata key, else the same name within 400 m; a row that matches nothing adds nothing.

candidates.note: Open (open.canada.ca lists Inuit communities under OGL-Canada); the map service did not answer a layer query from the sandbox.

candidates.name: Northwest Territories and Nunavut open data portals
candidates.note: opendata.gov.nt.ca returned 502 and gov.nu.ca 403 to automated access (not worked around). The territories are covered by federal sources instead: CGNDB names, CPCAD protected areas, StatCan's census subdivisions and postal areas, NRCan's road network with address ranges (3 MB and 1.6 MB), Inuit and First Nations communities, federal property and contaminated sites (4,486 in Nunavut).

candidates.name: CanVec 1:50,000 hydrography for BC, Ontario, Québec, NL, NWT and Nunavut; CanVec trails
candidates.note: Open, but 1.1 to 6.4 GB per province or territory (the 1:250,000 edition carries no names); would need a prepared, cached slice. CanVec's trails carry no names. The National Hydro Network's names reach the packs through CanVec where it is small enough.

candidates.name: NCES Common Core of Data before 2015-16 and IPEDS closed colleges
candidates.note: Open; the CCD's older directory files have addresses but the EDGE geocodes start in 2015-16, so the older years would need the geocoder.

candidates.name: Street-renaming lists of DC, Toronto and Baton Rouge
candidates.note: No open DC or Toronto renaming dataset was found; Baton Rouge's (public domain, 880 changes since the 1950s) has dates but no positions and would need matching to street lines. Chicago's portal terms are rejected.

candidates.name: Canada: Environment and Climate Change Canada Weatheradio transmitters
candidates.note: The Canadian counterpart of NOAA Weather Radio; its transmitter list must be found as a data file and its licence checked.

candidates.name: State and county election offices' polling place lists
candidates.note: Many states and counties publish the current election's polling places as open data; each must be checked for its licence and added with its election date.

candidates.name: California ABC alcoholic beverage licences (statewide)
candidates.licence: ABC Conditions of Use: 'considered in the public domain'
candidates.note: About 90,000 licences, but there is no bulk file: only web reports by county and type. Usable once a downloadable file is published (addresses only; the NAD covers California).

candidates.name: Small city alcohol, grocery and business licence lists (Grand Junction CO, Aspen CO, Corona CA)
candidates.note: Open but under 2,000 places each; Grand Junction and Aspen are in Colorado, which the NAD leaves out, so only layers with their own points can be used. Add one by one after checking each layer's fields.

candidates.name: Concept3D interactive campus maps (api.concept3d.com locations and categories)
candidates.licence: none stated; facts of the organisations' own maps
candidates.note: Used by hundreds of colleges, hospitals, zoos and cities; its public data (accessible entrances, parking, elevators, buildings) is what its own web maps read, with a public key built into its script. api.concept3d.com's robots.txt says "User-agent: * Disallow: /" (27 November 2026), so by the standing rule nothing is read for the published packs. The collector (placepacks/mapvendors/concept3d.py) is ready and the discovery records every Concept3D map id; NEEDS THE OWNER'S DECISION: an explicit override (registry robots_override) or the personal-use-only layer.

candidates.name: Other campus and indoor map vendors (Nuvo/CampusBird, Rave, Mappedin, Atrius/LocusLabs, MapsIndoors, Pointr, Jibestream, Mapwize, Mapsted, ArcGIS Indoors viewers)
candidates.note: In the registry with their fingerprints (placepacks/mapvendors/registry.py), so the discovery records which organisations use them; no collector yet: their data needs a customer key or login (Rave, Mappedin, LocusLabs, MapsIndoors, Pointr, Jibestream) or was not looked at (CampusBird, Mapwize, Mapsted). Malls' and airports' indoor directories are queue item Q3.

candidates.name: State pre-K program lists and adult education provider lists
candidates.note: Quick sweep 27 November 2026: no national open list with positions or NCES ids. Public pre-K classes are part of the CCD schools (grades PK); adult education providers are partly in IPEDS. State lists (for example state pre-K site finders) would be added one by one after checking each layer's fields and licence.

candidates.name: Section 1557 nondiscrimination notices (disability assistance contact lines) as data
candidates.note: Looked for 27 November 2026: published only as each provider's web page or PDF, not as a dataset; the hospital pages collector picks up accessibility desk phone numbers from hospitals' own accessibility pages instead.

candidates.name: Magnet school status (NCES CCD)
candidates.note: No longer in the CCD school files (2024-25); would come back if NCES publishes it again.

candidates.name: PREIT mall directories (preit.com)
candidates.note: Property pages answered 403 on 27 November 2026 (the sitemap answered); checked monthly by the malls workflow.

candidates.name: Washington Prime Group mall directories (wpgus.com)
candidates.note: The site's TLS certificate did not verify on 27 November 2026; checked monthly by the malls workflow.

candidates.name: Federal Realty and Kimco open-air centre tenant lists
candidates.note: Their property lists are script-only applications (no directory in the pages); their centres' own websites are read by the independent malls units.

candidates.name: Mappedin indoor maps of malls (Macerich, Brookfield, Tanger)
candidates.note: Mappedin Web reads api-gateway.mappedin.com with the customer's key; no public endpoint (27 November 2026).

candidates.name: Airport websites that refuse programs (Atlanta, Denver, Los Angeles, Austin, Nashville)
candidates.note: 403 or an anti-bot challenge page on 27 November 2026; recorded as blocked by the airports workflow each month, never got round.

candidates.name: BART, CTA and LA Metro elevator lists
candidates.note: No static elevator list published as data was found on 27 November 2026 (BART's API gives only current outages with a public demo key; CTA's 'L' stop list has an ADA column per station; LA Metro publishes a status page). Their GTFS feeds' pathways and wheelchair_boarding, where given, are read by gtfs-station-features. CTA's station ADA list could be added as station notes.

candidates.name: Museums whose websites refuse programs (Metropolitan Museum of Art, Art Institute of Chicago, Smithsonian museums)
candidates.note: 403 on 27 November 2026; recorded as blocked by the museum-access workflow each month, never got round. Permission letters could be sent (as for the blocked state tourism offices).
